body:
## Summary

Add a standalone, dependency-free Rust library for the bounded node #94
per-fill fee producer and six-word fee-ledger transition established by the
five retained fee evidence packets.

Target: Linux x86-64 node #94,
`3b7179cd967d1b13b683e05debfc685ad4c750e918226402d5d575eff1c0459f`.

The existing repository had independently validated fee packets and static
evaluators, but no reusable typed Rust implementation of their shared
per-fill behavior. This PR adds `src/node94-fees/` without importing the
unlicensed reference implementation or adding a root Cargo workspace.

## Implemented boundary

- typed perp and spot per-fill APIs with target maker/taker and current/previous
  rate selection;
- observed volume tiers, discount/referrer boundaries, builder tiers, rebates,
  deployer/protocol splits, and exempt-address behavior;
- target-ordered binary64 operations only where the evidence requires them,
  including explicit saturating/truncating integer conversion;
- typed `V U C r F T` fee ledger and collected-builder map, with deterministic
  creation/update order when payer, builder, and referrer alias;
- explicit unresolved-input errors and observable target saturation/floor
  events;
- bounded unit conversion, rate-grid point validation, and deployer-scale
  validation from the supporting packets.

The evidence README records the exact claims, target ranges, oracle counts,
coverage, reproduction commands, and unresolved dependencies. The crate README
documents the public contract and deliberately conservative field names.

## Evidence and comparison

Fresh oracle generation reproduced all stored evaluator data byte-for-byte:

- trade fee: 2,840 vectors;
- fill ledger: 1,015 vectors;
- fee scale: 3,613 vectors;
- rate grid: 2,749 vectors;
- unit conversion: 3,436 vectors.

All 207 targeted Python packet tests pass. The Rust suite transcribes all 13
named producer examples and adds adversarial boundary, aliasing, creation,
underflow/overflow, non-finite, and unresolved-input cases.

## Verification

- `cargo +1.94.1 test --locked --manifest-path src/node94-fees/Cargo.toml`
  (16/16 test functions pass)
- the same test suite passes on repository Rust 1.95.0
- Rust 1.94.1 locked release build passes
- Rust 1.94.1 fmt check passes
- Rust 1.94.1 clippy `-D warnings` passes
- library coverage: 711/835 executable lines (85.15%), 927/1,107 regions
  (83.74%)
- `make verify` passes
- `make catalogue-check` passes
- `make reproduce` passes

The repository-wide `make test` is not clean on the authoring macOS host:
GNU-binutils-dependent tests cannot find `objdump`/`readelf`, several existing
static-evaluator tests fail outside this component, and the run was eventually
terminated by signal 9 in `test_node_port_static`. `make doctor` reports the
same unavailable GNU binutils and optional Java/Ghidra tooling. No captured
node binary was executed.

## Deliberate limits

This does **not** claim a full fee schedule, 14-day rollover, production
exchange/collection ledger, live persistence layout, node #115 parity, ABI
identity, or whole-component binary identity. It intentionally excludes the
still-open spot/perp settlement and collection work. The repository fee
progress gates remain unchanged.
